edges.description: Occlusion of the glomerular capillaries is what collapses filtration to the point of oligoanuria, the renal outcome that decides whether dialysis is needed. The cited model of HUS pathogenesis puts glomerular thrombi upstream of renal shutdown.

Glomerular endothelial injury and the podocyte involvement that accompanies it breach the filtration barrier, which is what admits protein to the urine. Left uncited: the cited sources establish the glomerular lesion and list proteinuria among the renal sequelae, but none of them measures urinary protein against the lesion, so no quote in this entry supports the step itself.
Occlusion of the glomerular microvasculature is what produces the acute renal failure of the triad.
Erythrocytes are fragmented as they pass the occluded, fibrin-laden capillaries.
Platelets are consumed within the thrombi forming in the occluded capillaries.
Mechanical fragmentation of erythrocytes is the basis of the anaemia in this syndrome.
The fragmented erythrocytes produced by shearing are what appear on the blood film as schistocytes.
Platelet consumption within microvascular thrombi produces the thrombocytopenia.

Cerebral microvascular involvement is taken to produce the encephalopathy and seizures of severe disease. Left uncited and marked indirect: the cited sources report how often neurological involvement occurs and that it drives acute mortality, which is phenotype frequency rather than mechanism, so no quote in this entry establishes the step itself.

nodes.description: Shiga toxin activates the alternative complement pathway locally on the glomerular endothelial surface. There is no inherited regulator lesion here, which is what distinguishes this disease from atypical HUS; instead the toxin reduces factor H binding at the endothelial surface, so local regulation fails where the toxin has acted. In a mouse model expressing the toxin receptor only in podocytes, toxin challenge reduced podocyte VEGF-A, stripped the glomerular endothelial glycocalyx, lowered inhibitory factor H binding and activated complement locally - and early C5 inhibition rescued the phenotype.

nodes.description: Giving antibiotics during the diarrhoeal prodrome is associated with progression to HUS, which is why antibiotics are not recommended in suspected or confirmed STEC infection. The association is significant in low-risk-of-bias studies but not in the pooled set as a whole, and the proposed mechanism - induction of the bacterial SOS response and phage-mediated toxin release - is not established by these clinical data.

nodes.description: The prodromal illness is diarrhoea that typically begins non-bloody and becomes bloody over one to three days, reflecting the haemorrhagic colitis produced by colonic colonisation. nodes.description: A substantial minority of survivors carry chronic kidney disease. Kidney sequelae were present at five-year follow-up in 31% of children with STEC-HUS in the Polish national registry, although progression to stage 5 disease has become exceptional. No frequency band is set: the 31% figure is for "kidney sequelae", which the companion review defines as spanning reduced GFR, proteinuria, hypertension, chronic kidney disease and end-stage disease, so it is broader than this node and would overstate it.

nodes.description: Ingested STEC colonises the colon. Enterohaemorrhagic strains carry the locus of enterocyte effacement, whose intimin adhesin and type III secretion system produce attaching-and-effacing lesions that bring the organism into intimate contact with the epithelium. This is the site at which toxin is delivered to the host, and the lesion underlies the haemorrhagic colitis of the prodrome.

nodes.description: Intravenous fluid given in the first four days of diarrhoea, before HUS is established, is associated with a lower rate of oligoanuric renal failure. Children who became oligoanuric had received less intravenous fluid and sodium in that window. This is an observational association from a prospective cohort, not a randomised result, and the authors describe the intervention as underused.

evidence.snippet: Intravenous volume expansion is an underused intervention that could decrease the frequency of oligoanuric renal failure in patients at risk of HUS.

nodes.description: Terminal complement inhibition is supported mechanistically - toxin-driven complement activation is part of the lesion, and early C5 inhibition rescues a mouse model - but is not standard care. The phase 3 randomised placebo-controlled trial in 100 children found no effect on the acute phase and a lower proportion with renal sequelae at one year. The two results belong together: the acute primary endpoint was negative, and the one-year difference is a follow-up result the trial's own authors frame as needing larger studies. The abstract lists its secondary endpoints as haematologic and extrarenal involvement, so the one-year sequelae figure is not described there as one of them.

nodes.description: Erythrocytes are sheared as they traverse the occluded, fibrin-laden microvasculature and appear on the blood film as fragments. The haemolysis is mechanical rather than immune, which is the basis of the negative direct Coombs test used to separate it from immune haemolysis; no reference cached for this entry states that, so it is recorded here as an uncited standard-practice point rather than as a sourced claim.

nodes.description: Damage to the ribosome activates the stress-activated protein kinases p38 and JNK, inducing primary response genes, C-X-C chemokines including interleukin-8, and caspase-dependent apoptosis. This is the arm by which toxin kills target cells and recruits inflammation, as distinct from the sublethal gene-reprogramming arm that makes endothelium thrombogenic.

nodes.description: The toxin is an AB5 holotoxin: a pentamer of B subunits binds the neutral glycosphingolipid globotriaosylceramide (Gb3/CD77) on the target cell surface. Gb3 density differs markedly between vascular beds, and endothelial sensitivity to the toxin tracks that density, which is what targets the toxin to the glomerular endothelium and sets the organ tropism of the disease. The podocyte is bound here on the strength of PMID:37863058, whose human biopsy arm and title put the podocyte among the toxin's targets. Do not read it off that paper's mouse alone: Gb3 was engineered into podocytes there, so the model shows what podocyte-restricted receptor does, not that human podocytes carry it.

evidence.snippet: The presence of Gb3 targets Stx to the glomerular endothelium, where it causes major vascular injury. Endothelial cells from different vascular beds display varying degrees of sensitivity to Stx due, in large part, to the level of Gb3 expression.

nodes.description: Toxin released in the gut lumen crosses the intestinal epithelium into the systemic circulation. Toxin acting on the epithelium itself also triggers a ribotoxic stress response there, inducing chemokines and apoptosis. The identity of the systemic carrier of the toxin in blood remains unsettled, so the delivery step is the least well established link in this chain.

nodes.description: Supportive management is the mainstay: there is no approved antitoxin and no specific treatment of proven benefit in the acute phase. It comprises attention to volume status, electrolyte and acid-base management, blood pressure control, transfusion as needed, and renal replacement therapy when the kidney injury demands it.

evidence.reference_title: New insights into Shiga toxin-mediated endothelial dysfunction in hemolytic uremic syndrome
evidence.snippet: Patients currently receive supportive care to manage symptoms, as no specific treatment exists for D+HUS.

nodes.description: Toxin-stimulated glomerular and umbilical-vein endothelial cells secrete ultra-large von Willebrand factor multimeric strings, to which perfused platelets adhere immediately. The toxin additionally delays ADAMTS13 cleavage of those strings, so the platelet-decorated multimers persist. Note that plasma ADAMTS13 activity in this disease is within the normal range - the defect is local and toxin-imposed, not the systemic protease deficiency of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura.
